newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends steady in shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends steady in shortcovering.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady on Thursday because of mild shortcovering and on the back of firm prices in Japan, dealers said.

"There was a little bit done here and there as some players engaged in some shortcovering. But it was nothing special and you could even say the market was in a quiet frame of mind," a local rubber trader said.

Traders said firm prices in Japan helped shore up sentiment among local dealers. Tokyo's benchmark April contract recovered from a morning fall to end unchanged at 142.9 yen while Kobe's April contract closed at 143.4 yen against the previous 142.8.
"The market is still relatively flat. The shortcovering allowed prices to hold at their current levels," another rubber trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 126.00-127.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 126.75 cents.
December RSS1 was seen at 180.00-181.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg from 181.00 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 178.50 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg from the previous 178.25 cents.
